steps.content:
December, N.F. 113
After the BR-002 High Tower Black Ring Crisis

MBCC Chief's Office
The Black Ring crisis has finally concluded against all odds, but the troubles hidden beneath never truly cease. Just as old problems are resolved, new ones emerge.

West District's reconstruction is a pressing matter. Months of backlogged documents have piled into a heap on the desk. If this office ever experiences a brief moment of peace, it's merely a prelude to the next knock on the door.
Just like today...
On your desk lies a dark web investigation report from the 9th Agency. At the top, an anonymous account stands out conspicuously.

steps.speaker: 9th Agency
steps.content: This account was registered approximately one week ago. Initially showing no suspicious activity, it began frequently logging in two days ago to browse and post in numerous sensitive forums as well as download data.

steps.speaker: 9th Agency
steps.content: We've extracted its search keywords. The account shows particular interest in Black Rings and Mania phenomena. After viewing each batch of information, it offers high prices to purchase the related documents.
Advanced Theoretical Studies on Mania, The Black Ring: Comprehensive Analysis and Potential Crisis Assessment, Underground Hypercube Research and Utilization Protocols...
Every single transaction revolved exclusively around Mania. Underground experiment logs, document fragments, unsigned research notes... This person hoards everything and is ready to pay generously.
..."Collect the latest BR-002 samples on site"? It's even issued a bounty?

steps.speaker: 9th Agency
steps.content: Yes. However, as of now, no one has responded to the bounty. Even professional contractors from the dark web must ask themselves whether the money is worth dying for.
The agent from the 9th Agency pauses briefly, then points to a highlighted entry in the report.

steps.speaker: 9th Agency
steps.content: What concerns us more is that it's showing equally strong interest in <color=#fb9259>Quinn and West District's latest activity</color>. The Outlands have long wanted to meddle with the new mine, and now with unknown individuals stirring things up on the dark web, we must exercise extra caution.

steps.speaker: 9th Agency
steps.content: Additionally, since yesterday evening, a new keyword has appeared in this anonymous account's searches.
<color=#fb9259>"MBCC Chief"</color>... Looks like it's taken an interest in me as well.

steps.speaker: 9th Agency
steps.content: Yes, Chief. Beyond the Bureau's public records, it's also searching for your personal information and background history.

steps.speaker: 9th Agency
steps.content: But no new transaction posts so far. We've applied quadruple encryption to all your information online. Currently, it can only access content that's already available to the public.

steps.speaker: 9th Agency
steps.content: They're very cautious. The account is encrypted through the dark web, making it difficult to trace with our current technology. Investigation will take time.

BR-002 was just over. West District can't afford another blow now. You need to nip this threat in the bud. If this can't be achieved with tech, it's time to switch to a more primitive and direct approach.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: Since this person has now turned their attention to me, why not give them what they want and use that as our way in?
After a few seconds of contemplation, you look up and speak calmly but assertively.

options: I need you to do me a favor.

choices.text: I need you to do me a favor.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: Get an anonymous account ready for me as soon as possible. Make sure it's not too recently registered and looks "natural" enough that it won't appear suspicious.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: When they come online next time, I'll deal with them personally.
The 9th Agency is highly efficient. In less than twenty minutes, they've already sent the anonymous dark web account you requested to your device.
The account was registered about six months ago, with the gender and IP location strategically exposed. Most of its bookmarks are posts related to the MBCC Chief.
The dark web is chaotic as always. People are always talking, trading, arguing, their voices ultimately drowning in a dizzying flood of information.

You quickly locate the forum where the mysterious account is most active and cast your bait: a tip about your current whereabouts, accompanied by several candid photos taken from questionable angles—blurry, but close enough to be enticing.
You don't turn off your device, but instead turn the notification volume to the max before returning to your work, patiently waiting for your target to take the bait.
Two hours later, you hear a chime. The forum notifies you that your account has received a new private message.
<color=#fb9259>Anon</color>: Hello, I was wondering if those photos were taken by you in the post you published two hours ago?
The fish has taken the bait.

options: Hello. Yes, they were taken by me. Why?

choices.text: Hello. Yes, they were taken by me. Why?

steps.content:
<color=#fb9259>Anon</color>: Nothing. Just a little curious about them. Are those people from the MBCC? I think I spotted their logo.

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: You can tell even from those photos? You must know a thing or two about the MBCC.

<color=#fb9259>Anon</color>: It's not that hard to make out. I'm just guessing from certain details... But I'd like to confirm, is that person the MBCC's Chief?
You pause for a moment. Their response is tactful, deflecting the question back to you without revealing anything about themselves. Just as the 9th Agency said, this person is relentlessly cautious.

options: Yes. So, you're interested in this Chief too?

choices.text: Yes. So, you're interested in this Chief too?

steps.content: <color=#fb9259>Anon</color>: Yes. I am indeed curious about him, so I've been gathering all kinds of information.
steps.female_content: <color=#fb9259>Anon</color>: Yes. I am indeed curious about her, so I've been gathering all kinds of information.

steps.content: Their response continues to give away nothing. Going on with this usual, roundabout approach will likely lead you nowhere. You need to try a more direct strategy.
<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: What a coincidence. I see you've saved quite a few posts about Chief as well. Since we seem to share an interest, why don't we keep in touch and trade info?

This time, they remain silent for a full five minutes. You worry you've overplayed your hand, and begin rehearsing what excuse might sound convincing enough when they inevitably ask what you're really after.
But the message that finally appears on your screen leaves you wide-eyed.

<color=#fb9259>Anon</color>: Would you mind clarifying what you mean precisely by "keeping in touch"?

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: ...?
You read and reread this short line of text, unable to grasp what they're actually asking. Thankfully, their explanation follows immediately.
<color=#fb9259>Anon</color>: Using what means? At what frequency? Any rules? Should we use secret codes to prevent leaks?

Orderly, structured, and utterly precise. This barrage of unexpected questions immediately reminds you of a research survey. Rather than the sly probing of a dark web veteran, it feels more like... a rigid assessment by a scholar?
There's no time to analyze further. You gingerly cobble together vague answers to the questions. Just as you think you've successfully dodged the interrogation, they send another message.
<color=#fb9259>Anon</color>: I see. I'd like to confirm something else. How did you manage to take photos from that distance? Who are you? Do you know Chief personally?

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: I'm a sheriff. I took these photos while on a mission with Chief.

<color=#fb9259>Anon</color>: Sheriff? May I ask which precinct? What's your work ID? Your rank? And when and where exactly were these photos taken? Did you take them for the mission, or for some other reason?

Unconsciously, you wipe sweat from your brow. You thought assuming an official identity would dispel any further doubts, but you're instantly bombarded with specific details you can't possibly fabricate convincingly.

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: ...Actually, I'm a journalist.

<color=#fb9259>Anon</color>: Journalist? Which media do you work for? Where are your articles published? What story are you currently investigating? Can you specify the camera model you used to take these photos?

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: ...My true identity is a dark web assassin.

<color=#fb9259>Anon</color>: Assassin? Is Chief your target then? Who hired you? How much do you charge? If you could get this close, why haven't you made your move yet?

<color=#fb9259>Anon</color>: Assassin? Is Chief your target then? Who hired you? How much do you charge? If you could get this close, why haven't you made your move yet?

Just a little over ten minutes of "interrogation" have thrown you into what feels like a silent battlefield. The stubborn, relentless questioning from the other side of the screen is even harder to defend against than actual weapons.

Overwhelmed by your predicament, you don't even notice when Wynn enters the room. Coffee pot in hand, she refills your empty cup skillfully, then spends a moment studying your screen before suddenly blurting out something.

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: Why not just say you're a fan? "Number one fan from the Eastside MBCC Chief Fan Club" or something.
You freeze momentarily, almost convinced you misheard. But there's no time to hesitate now, so you type out the frankly absurd identity.

options: I'm President of the Eastside MBCC Chief Fan Club.

choices.text: I'm President of the Eastside MBCC Chief Fan Club.

steps.content: You wait anxiously for their response. After a while, a message finally appears.

<color=#fb9259>Anon</color>: A fan club? Sorry, I'm not familiar with these kinds of organizations. What exactly do you do?

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: We collect and share everything related to Chief, of course. Chief is such an enigmatic figure. We have all kinds of fans in our group. Theorists, researchers, you name it.
With Wynn coaching you, you're now handling the conversation with ease. Interview recordings, speech videos, gossip articles... You fire off all the "evidence" she's feeding you.

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: And that's not all! We also make our official fan club merch: limited-edition badges, collectible postcards, Chief's briefcase replicas, mini Chief keychains... You name it, we've got it!
You stop abruptly.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: ...Wait, do these things actually exist?
You turn to Wynn with a suspicious look, but she just innocently shrugs her shoulders.

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: Faye takes care of all that. I don't really know the details. You'll have to ask her yourself.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: ...Forget it. I'll deal with her about this later.
The "typing..." message keeps flashing at the top of the chat window, but no new text appears. Clearly, they're still hesitating about how to respond.
You're just one step away from gaining their trust. You make your finishing move with confidence.
<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: Young people are into this stuff these days. You seriously don't know? How old are you anyway? Don't you go on the normal side of the internet sometimes?
Finally, the message notification chimes.

<color=#fb9259>Anon</color>: ...I see.

<color=#fb9259>Anon</color>: I'm not familiar with what young people are interested in these days. Please excuse my ignorance.

<color=#fb9259>Anon</color>: I live in a satellite town and work as an independent scientist, primarily studying Mania phenomena.

<color=#fb9259>Anon</color>: I rarely go out, so I don't keep up with these popular trends.
They seem to feel obligated to reciprocate after you shared your supposed identity.
But how would an independent scientist have so much money to splurge on intel from the dark web? At least come up with something more convincing...

After a moment's hesitation, you reexamine the 9th Agency's investigation report. This account has indeed purchased substantial amounts of intel, but you can tell that many of these expensive leads are, in fact, false information.

You thought this might be some mysterious organization with deep pockets and powerful connections. Now it seems more like an easy, wealthy target being circled by predators. No wonder rumors about it are everywhere on the dark web.
While you're still processing this, several new messages suddenly pop up. They seem to think you're still doubting their identity and hastily provide more explanation.

<color=#fb9259>Anon</color>: I'm only interested in that Chief because I heard he's an expert in the field of Mania. I have no other intentions.

<color=#fb9259>Anon</color>: The Ring Research Institute is hard enough to get into, and coming from a satellite town means I practically have no chance. But even so, I don't want to give up... Finding ways to defend against disasters is a topic that concerns every researcher.

<color=#fb9259>Anon</color>: Please rest assured, I'll keep any information about him confidential, and I promise I won't do anything that could harm him in any way.
steps.female_content:
<color=#fb9259>Anon</color>: I'm only interested in that Chief because I heard she's an expert in the field of Mania. I have no other intentions.

<color=#fb9259>Anon</color>: The Ring Research Institute is hard enough to get into, and coming from a satellite town means I practically have no chance. But even so, I don't want to give up... Finding ways to defend against disasters is a topic that concerns every researcher.

<color=#fb9259>Anon</color>: Please rest assured, I'll keep any information about her confidential, and I promise I won't do anything that could harm her in any way.

steps.content: On the screen, the stilted explanations continue popping up, each line bearing an excessive seriousness. You stare at the words, the corners of your mouth tightening slightly.
They seem quite... stubborn. It's hard to tell whether this is naive single-mindedness or a calculated facade.
Suddenly, a notification flashes at the top of the chat window. The next moment, you see they've disabled their anonymity setting.
A strange profile picture appears, and a new username catches your eye.
Archivist 19260817
You catch yourself holding your breath. Dropping anonymity voluntarily? Do they truly mean to get candid, or do they have an ulterior motive?
Regardless, this unexpected act of frankness still causes a slight tremor in your otherwise guarded composure.

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: I believe you. But if you're so interested, why not contact the MBCC and try to schedule a meeting with Chief in person?

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: ...Maybe someday.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: I'll try when I'm truly ready.
You stare at the brief reply, your expression darkening slightly.

Just as the 9th Agency reported, they're extremely cautious. They clearly take an interest in "Chief," yet the moment you suggested a meeting in person, they immediately retreated behind their defenses.
But on the other hand, you don't think they're particularly calculating either, like right now...

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: Alright, then just join Chief's fan club for now. It's the fastest way to get the latest updates about Chief.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: Is that so?

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: Okay. How do I join?
Hook, line, and sinker. They even meticulously arrange ways to stay in regular contact with you, and decide on a "secret code."
Even the 9th Agency agent silently observing nearby can no longer suppress a smile.

steps.speaker: 9th Agency
steps.content: At the 9th Agency, such amateur tradecraft could get an agent sent back to the academy by the superiors.
You merely raise an eyebrow without responding, your gaze fixed on the now-silent chat window on the screen.
That marks the end of the first exchange. It went smoothly, yet it feels like you've merely lifted the corner of an unknown curtain, revealing even more elusive shadows behind it.
Who exactly is this mysterious <color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>? Are they really a cautious, budding independent scientist? Or is it all a carefully crafted facade?
And why are they so eager to collect information about Black Rings, Mania, and you?

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: Keep this account active and continue monitoring.
This chess match is far from over. To unravel these mysteries, you need to maintain contact with them and find the answers through careful probing.
